note: V2 companion file. It adds the FY2023 comparative year and the FY2024 line items the V2 models need, and it does NOT restate anything already in caterpillar_fy2024.json - every key here is either a new key for FY2024 or a figure for FY2023. That file is a protected regression fixture and stays byte-identical.
data_source: SEC XBRL company-facts API, CIK 0000018230, form 10-K. Every figure below was pulled from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000018230.json and is the filer's own tagged extraction from its 10-K - a primary source, not a standardised third-party restatement.
cross_check: The same pull reproduces the FY2024 figures already in caterpillar_fy2024.json exactly: Revenues 64,809, CostOfRevenue 40,199, OperatingIncomeLoss 13,072, NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic 10,792, RetainedEarningsAccumulatedDeficit 59,352, StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest 19,494, NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities 12,035. Total debt 38,409 reconciles as ShortTermBorrowings 4,393 + LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths 6,665 + LongTermDebtNoncurrent 27,351. Capital expenditure 3,215 reconciles as PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment 1,988 + PaymentsToAcquireEquipmentOnLease 1,227. An exact tie on seven independently tagged figures is the evidence that the FY2023 figures below are on the same basis.

expected.note: Known-healthy public manufacturer with two clean years. The F-Score misses exactly two tests - long-term debt rose from 24,472 to 27,351 and revenue fell from 67,060 to 64,809 against a flat asset base - which is what a reader of the 10-K would predict.

derivations.total_debt_2023: 37,878 = ShortTermBorrowings 4,643 + LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths 8,763 + LongTermDebtNoncurrent 24,472. The same three-part reconciliation reproduces the FY2024 figure of 38,409 already in the V1 file exactly, which is why this composition is used rather than a different one.
derivations.capital_expenditure_2023: 3,092 = PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment 1,597 + PaymentsToAcquireEquipmentOnLease 1,495. Caterpillar splits capital expenditure across two lines because equipment leased to customers is a distinct programme. The same sum reproduces the FY2024 figure of 3,215 in the V1 file exactly.
derivations.gross_profit_2023: 24,293 = revenue 67,060 - cogs 42,767. Caterpillar does not tag GrossProfit; the identity is definitional and the FY2024 file records the same relationship (64,809 - 40,199 = 24,610).
derivations.net_income_2023: 10,335, NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic - profit attributable to common shareholders. ProfitLoss (including non-controlling interests) is 10,332; the two differ by the -3 attributable to non-controlling interests. The V1 file uses the attributable figure for FY2024 (10,792 against a ProfitLoss of 10,788), so the same basis is used here. income_continuing_ops carries ProfitLoss, which is the measure Beneish TATA wants.
derivations.share_price_2024: 371.4752 = market_value_equity 177,528 (already in the V1 file) / shares_outstanding 477.9. Derived from figures already in the project rather than quoting a market close, so the whole chain stays reproducible from one source. It is used only to express the DCF's implied value as an upside or downside; no analysis depends on it.
derivations.interest_expense_2023: DELIBERATELY OMITTED. Caterpillar tags no interest expense concept anywhere in its XBRL company facts - the income-statement line 'Interest expense excluding Financial Products' is not separately tagged, and InterestPaidNet (1,435 for FY2023) is cash paid, not expense. Rather than substitute a cash figure for an accrual one, the file omits it: interest coverage is reported for FY2024 and omitted for FY2023, and the trend block therefore has nothing to compare. Same discipline as the Vodafone Idea EBIT omission in V1.
